messages:
priya: Quick update — I ran a focused regional benchmark for the 40B quantized model using slab-tiling vs tiling kernels across h100 (us-west, eu-west) and a100 (us-west, ap-southeast). Heatmap + raw csv uploaded: https://redwood-gcs/bench/174555
mike: Nice. TL;DR numbers?
priya: TL;DR below (median / p99 / tokens/s). short run, mixed load (simulated PLG burst).

h100 us-west (slab-tiling): 48ms / 190ms / 380 tps
h100 eu-west (slab-tiling): 52ms / 210ms / 360 tps
a100 us-west (tiling): 65ms / 350ms / 280 tps
a100 ap-southeast (tiling): 72ms / 430ms / 250 tps

Observations: slab-tiling on h100 gives ~25% better tail and ~30% better throughput vs a100 tiling for this workload. a100 shows higher variance and longer p99, especially APAC (thermal throttling + kernel fallback in later sequences).

Also ran a hybrid run (slotting h100 + a100 fallback). Fallback increases p99 by ~1.6x but keeps throughput from collapsing.

priya: kernel notes: slab-tiling reduces KV cache pressure for long-context use (8k+); tiling has slightly lower median in some short-context cases but worse tail under burst.

oliver: For reserved pools what concurrency targets are you thinking per GPU?
priya: Based on the sim and safety buffer, recommended steady concurrency targets: h100 -> 14 concurrent requests (avg seq len ~512), a100 -> 9. Autoscale headroom: keep 1.8x warm buffer for day spikes, 2.5x for night APAC bursts (observed 2.2x peak in sim). Reserve margin: +15% capacity for canary rollouts.
jamie: Ops check — how long to warm slab caches? impact on cold starts?
priya: Warmup priming ~60s per slot under representative traffic, full KV warm ~5–7 minutes for heavy contexts. We saw tail spikes during first 3 mins if no priming. Recommendation: pre-warm slots during deploy windows using ramped synthetic traffic (script attached).

mike: Can you paste the priming command?
priya: Sure:
```bash
# quick priming loop for pool N GPUs
for i in $(seq 1 100); do
  curl -s -X POST $REDWOOD_API/generate -d '{"model":"40b-q","input":"prime token sequence ..."}' &
done
wait
```

jamie: Got it. For capacity planning — any concrete GPU counts for a medium tenant (SLA: 75 qps, 99th latency < 300ms)?
oliver: Quick calc: assume 75 qps * avg tokens per request 150 -> ~11250 tokens/s needed. Use measured tokens/s per GPU: h100 slab ~380 -> need ceil(11250/380)=30 GPUs; with 1.8x headroom -> 54 GPUs reserved. For a100 (280 tps) -> 41 GPUs -> with 1.8x -> 74 GPUs. Recommend mixed pool: 40 h100 + 16 a100 to hit cost/availability constraints, with 20% buffer for rollouts.
mike: That mix seems reasonable. Any region split recs?
priya: If traffic is US-heavy (70%): split US-west 70% of pool; eu 20%; apac 10%. Keep failover policy to spill APAC to EU before US if APAC capacity constrained to avoid intercontinental latency spikes.
jamie: I'll draft a provisioning PR for the reserved pool numbers and include the priming job in deploy playbook.
sre-bot: New grafana panel: https://grafana/redwood/d/bench/heatmap-174555 — auto-update every 5m :chart_with_upwards_trend:
mike: Perfect. Action items: (1) priya: add detailed csv + summary to bench doc, (2) oliver/jamie: draft reserved pool PR + warmup job, (3) ops: schedule canary with 15% reserved margin. :+1:
priya: On it. Thanks all.
